notes:
Summary: Firebreak builds low-latency trading decisioning and market-microstructure products. They need sub-50ms p99 inference for short prompt lengths (30-80 tokens) and high cost sensitivity at scale. Currently evaluating Redwood Dedicated + Optimize recommendations.

Recent activity/timeline:
- 2026-01-25: Intro call (AE Elena) — high level requirements, confirmed VPC requirement, initial throughput targets.
- 2026-02-11: Technical deep-dive (SE Marcus) — discussed KV/prefix caching, batching windows, and quantization tradeoffs. Fireflies: ff_2026-02-11_8921.
- 2026-02-18: Security questionnaire submitted; asked about KMS, audit logs, and data residency SLA. Drive: security FAQ.
- 2026-03-02: Onsite perf workshop (remote) — ran toy benchmarks, saw p50 ~18ms but p99 spikes 120-200ms under burst. Fireflies: ff_2026-03-02_9144.
- 2026-03-09: Pricing + architecture sync with Eng and Procurement; requested dedicated node sizing and cost per 1M tokens with int8 quantization.

Requirements & constraints:
- Workload: real-time decisioning (micro-batching influenced by market tick cadence), occasional chat/alerts for traders, reranking historical signals for signals pipeline.
- Latency SLOs: p99 < 50ms for 30-80 token responses; 95th < 25ms preferred during market hours.
- Throughput: baseline 150 req/s, burst to 1200 req/s for 30s windows during open auctions.
- Cost target: <$350k ARR; prefer lower unit $/1000 tokens via batching/quantization/caching.
- Model preferences: open models compatible with int8 quantization; must support KV cache eviction and short context optimization.
- Routing: need regional routing (NA primary) + fallback to warmed spare capacity; distro must be predictable.
- Deployment: VPC private control plane, customer-managed KMS for key rotation.

Engineering asks (Optimize interest):
- Quantization: evaluate int8 and mixed-precision kernels; produce accuracy vs perf matrix on their workloads.
- Batching: recommended dynamic batching window <6ms, adaptive based on market tick rate; want tooling to simulate bursts.
- Caching: prefix and KV cache for repeating prompt fragments and market context; TTL controls and eviction policies required.
- Benchmarking: 72h continuous perf run with synthetic replay of market traces + 3 load profiles (baseline, auction-burst, failure-recovery). Need deterministic harness and noise controls.
- Observability: token-level latency/cost breakdown, per-route SLO dashboards, and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

POC plan (proposed):
1) Provision Dedicated pool (2 config sizes) in their VPC with KMS integration.
2) Run 72h perf bench with redwood-provided harness using their market replay trace.
3) Compare profiles: fp16 baseline, int8 quantized, and hybrid; measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and accuracy/regression on 200 eval prompts.
4) Deliver report and recommended node sizing + autoscale policy and fallback routing.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We can tolerate tiny quality delta if it saves 40-60% cost per token" — Head of SRE.
- "p99 spikes kill our SLAs during auctions — need deterministic tail behavior." — CTO.

Open items / blockers: short benchmark runs are noisy; security needs SOC2 + KMS proof; procurement waiting on final cost model.

- Schedule 72h perf run (Owner: Elena) — target start 2026-03-20.
- SE to finalize harness + replay trace (Owner: Marcus).
- Security runbook handoff and KMS test credentials (Owner: Priya).
